entries.test: Public evidence of ChatGPT's contributions to scientific and medical advances and measured GDP and productivity gains through August 14, 2025 would test whether the promised transformation had occurred.
entries.note: The claim concerns a transformative impact, not the absence of any useful contributions.
This is a rhetorical contrast between publicity and scientific achievement.

entries.test: Altman's public prelaunch promises, GPT-5's demonstrated capabilities, and reporting and public reactions during the week after launch would test the claimed mismatch and its recognition.
entries.note: The public-recognition language has a plain reading as widespread recognition, not literal unanimity.
Underwhelming expresses an assessment of the release without specifying a performance claim.

entries.test: Public documentation of an AGI system's capabilities and development method would test whether scaling alone can reach AGI.
entries.note: The extracted claim endorses scaling's ultimate insufficiency; it is not merely a report of survey responses.

Marcus distinguishes media sentiment from investor sentiment without asserting a particular measurable change. The normalization turns his personal caution into advice and treats an illustrative bubble as established.
The Waterloo metaphor does not commit to a specific defeat or outcome.

entries.test: Altman's documented promises and public evaluations of GPT-5's general capabilities at launch would test the delivery and AGI claims.
entries.note: The emphatic wording asserts a substantive capability shortfall.

entries.test: Representative launch-period satisfaction surveys and documented customer requests to restore older models would test both assertions.
entries.note: Almost nobody is a strong prevalence claim, not merely a claim that complaints existed.

entries.test: Public polling and contemporaneous commentary would test whether many people had come to regard Altman's AI promises as deceptive salesmanship.
entries.note: Despite the colorful language, the sentence asserts a public perception rather than directly establishing fraud.

entries.test: Public capability evaluations of systems available by August 14, 2025 would test whether any lab had delivered AGI.
entries.note: The absence-of-AGI assertion is checkable. The accompanying description of Grok-4 and Llama-4 as underwhelming is evaluative.

The source says improvement is impossible under those conditions; the normalization says those actions cannot produce improvement. Drowning out critics and pouring good money after bad supply no shared operational test.

entries.test: Public research publications and demonstrations introducing substantively new AI approaches after the post would test the prediction of their emergence.
entries.note: The source predicts new approaches will arise; it does not explicitly predict that they will replace existing approaches.

entries.test: Public demonstration and independent evaluation of a system achieving AGI would settle the firm prediction of eventual arrival.
entries.note: Eventual arrival is asserted firmly. The next-decade timing is only a possibility, not a deadline.

entries.test: Public technical documentation of the systems that first achieve AGI would show whether LLMs were the leading approach.
entries.note: The preceding discussion supplies AGI as the destination. I think it is safe to say introduces a firm conclusion here.

entries.test: The cited METR study's methods and results, alongside relevant benchmark performance, would test the asserted gap between benchmark success and practical coding performance.
entries.note: Marcus endorses the study's purported finding in his own voice.
The trustworthy-AI outcome is explicitly only a possibility. The prediction that scientists will pursue new paths could be checked separately.
